item.title: Nagoya Castle: Golden Shachihoko and the Honmaru Palace — Guide
item.description: Nagoya Castle was built on the orders of Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1612 as the seat of the Owari branch of his family, and its keep — crowned with a pair of golden shachihoko, the mythical tiger-headed dolphins that became the symbol of the city — presides over broad moats and massive stone ramparts. The great prize of a visit today is the Honmaru Palace, destroyed in the war and painstakingly rebuilt using original techniques, its chambers lined with dazzling gold-leaf screens of tigers and pines and its fresh hinoki cypress halls among the finest examples of shoin-zukuri palace architecture anywhere in Japan.
